dossier.public_summary: The dip that appears near a 12.7-day period changes depth by more than a factor of ten between transits and between sectors, with one transit essentially flat. Such unstable depths match stellar variability and noise on an active 5-day rotator, not a steady planet transit.

reasons.why: Depths are inconsistent at very high sigma; one transit is ~5 sigma shallow, flagged as outlier, indicates only a few bad events not a consistent planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent=2.02331430779331e-08, depth 746 ppm vs 7259 ppm vs 9279 ppm

reasons.why: Depth changes within the same pipeline (TESS-SPOC) beyond errors; with only 3 sectors the signal dominates chi2, so signal is not steady where a planet must be.
reasons.value: p_constant=7.753e-9, verdict=changes_within_a_source, sector 46 depth_ppm=746 err=1071 vs sector 23 7259 vs QLP 91 9279

reasons.why: Combined strong evidence the dip depth is unstable, inconsistent with a planet transit that should be repeatable to within sector aperture differences.

M-dwarf rotates fast with large spotted variability; depth instability plus ~10.27 SNR and 3 short near-gap transits favours variability/noise over a planet; centroid inconclusive and neighbours plausible_within_1px=0 support no positive planet evidence to outweigh.
